Plot the Baseline Rate Distribution of a Fitted G2Gcov Model

Source: R/methods.R
plot_lambda0.Rd

Plots the Gamma mixing distribution of the latent baseline rate \(\lambda_0\), with all covariates equal to zero, implied by a model fitted with G2G_static_MLE (time-invariant covariates) or G2G_varying_MLE (time-varying covariates). The mean and median of \(\lambda_0\) are marked with vertical lines and shown in a second title.

Usage

plot_lambda0(solution, upper_q = 0.95)

Arguments

solution

A fitted model object of class "G2Gcov".

upper_q

Numeric quantile in (0, 1) used to set the upper x-axis limit. Default 0.95.

Value

Invisibly returns a list with the mean and median of \(\lambda_0\).

Details

In the G2G model, \(p_0 = 1 - e^{-\lambda_0}\), where \(\lambda_0\) follows a Gamma distribution with shape \(r\) and rate \(\alpha\). The fitted r and alpha are on the original covariate scale, so the curve describes a subject whose covariates are all zero, which can lie outside the range of the data. The mean and median have closed forms: \(r / \alpha\) and qgamma(0.5, shape = r, rate = alpha). When \(r < 1\) the density is unbounded at 0, so the curve rises steeply there and the mean lies above the median.

See also

plot_p0, G2G_static_MLE, G2G_varying_MLE

Examples

# \donttest{
  data(kb_data_sample)
  fit <- G2G_varying_MLE(Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp,
                         data = kb_data_sample, subject = "id")
  plot_lambda0(fit)

# }
